title: Diagrams and extensions: naming a structure inside another model
summary: Name every element of a structure to describe its embedded copies, then use compactness to construct proper countable elementary extensions.
abstract: How can axioms require a new model to contain a copy of a given structure? Give every original element a name and record the facts about those names. Recording atomic facts and their negations forces an embedded copy; recording every first-order fact forces a copy that preserves the truth of all formulas with original parameters. These collections are called diagrams. Combined with compactness, they show that every countably infinite structure in a countable language has a proper countable elementary extension. For the natural-number order, such an extension can contain a point above every original natural number while still having no greatest element. Finite structures admit no proper elementary extensions.
